classification.difficultyReason: Development: students compare the flat and 3D displays and explain how increased width and depth exaggerate a twofold sales difference. Connecting several visual dimensions to the false impression extends the taught critique of unsuitable representations through routine linked reasoning.

content.prompt: Look at the two graphs showing sales of two brands of TVs. Which graph is misleading, and why?

spec.description: Equal-width TV bars, X4000,Y8000. Zero baseline retained.

Source opaque front/top/right visible cuboid faces: X4000,Y8000 front heights, Y twice front width/depth. Outlines and source perspective preserved; front/back hidden edges are occluded by opaque faces.
spec.purposefulShading: Front/right fills are assessed three-dimensional chart faces; white top is an explicit face mask.
spec.geometryReview: Explicit visible faces; source-hashed silhouette/occlusion review pending.

answer.short: The right-hand 3D graph: unequal widths exaggerate Brand Y, and perspective makes heights harder to read.
answer.worked: Brand Y has twice the sales of Brand X. In the right-hand graph, Y is also wider and deeper, exaggerating the difference. The sloping top faces make the reading height unclear.
